coverage.content: Rubric age care/delay old age; backward reference to childhood; four broad ages with hot/moist growth to25/30, hot/dry sustained vigour to40/45, cold/dry weakening to60/65, cold/moist final decline attributed to weak natural heat/cold humours until death. Announces seven finer ages but names three and folds them into first broad age; no invented remaining names.

After7: good habits/controlled emotional environment and sleep; bath2–3weekly, feeding-play-feeding3daily and separate provisional drinking frequency; water-mixed wine, avoid cold water on food and milk/fruit/cheese stone risk. School with orderly teacher, no beating or excessive unwilling attendance; verbal teaching/correction.

After14 avoid excessive humours from excess food/drink; if excessive, bloodletting/mild medicines. Sexual restraint, marriage20/25. After25 stronger work, avoid hot/dry/red-bile foods, use cold/moist foods including fruit, diluted wine, avoid old strong wine; bloodletting/purging season/nature-dependent and relatively safe then.

After35, avoid bloodletting unless great need; prefer medicinal purging. Avoid intercourse/exertion/anger/anxious thought to delay ageing, seek joy, nourishing food/clear blood/good wine; bath1–2monthly. Original45 impression corrected to native35; treatment threshold not broad-age boundary.

Dry-cooked foods; fasting preserved myrobalan count with unit unclear, or named electuary/hot water. Full first preparation with myrobalan kinds, long pepper, iron scale from forging, sugar/honey. Second measured preparation10drams kebles,2iron scale,2.5agaric,1.5each ginger/black pepper/cloves; powder, mix honey/sugar, electuary. Daily/year morning fasting use, drink afterward, no definite wine noun, abstain food until midday; Avicenna authority.

Beyond65 avoid BOTH bloodletting and purging unless great need; easy nourishing foods, old red wine, avoid white/new/sweet wine. Moderate exertion/bathing/gentle rubbing, avoid cold, fumigate room/bed with uncertain first-name segmentation plus myrrh/amber/storax, named warming electuaries and all warm electuaries; end.
